simple.meaning: חֶדְוָה (chedvâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “rejoicing.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חֶדְוָה (H2304) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Chronicles 16:27, with occurrences in 1 Chronicles, Nehemiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֶדְוָה (H2304) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חֶדְוָה (H2304) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חֶדְוָה (chedvâh) / H2304 is traced through 1 Chronicles 16:27, Nehemiah 8:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2304. chedvah חֶדְוָה noun feminine (late) joy (Aramaic חדוא ). — ׳ח 1Chr 16:27 (in the sanctuary); י ׳חֶדְוַת Neh 8:10 (|| אַלתֵּֿעָצֵ֑בוּ ). חֶדְוָה noun feminine joy ( ᵑ7 Syriac; see Biblical Hebrew II. חדה ); — absolute ׳בְּח Ezra 6:16 with joy .

occurrences.englishText: Honor and majesty are before him.

Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of Yahweh is your strength.”
